direction: Assess this staff-engineer candidate for depth on distributed systems and for how they lead without authority. Probe specifics, not generalities; let them talk.

attendee.name: Priya
attendee.bio: Staff engineer, 9 years, last at a payments company.

speaker: me
text: Thanks for making the time, Priya. Want to start with what you're working on right now?

speaker: them
text: Sure. I lead the team that owns our ledger — the system of record for every money movement.

speaker: them
text: Last year we re-architected it from a single Postgres to a sharded, event-sourced design.

speaker: me
text: That's a big change. What forced it?

speaker: them
text: We were hitting write-throughput limits during peak, and reconciliation was taking hours.

speaker: them
text: Honestly the hardest part wasn't the tech, it was getting three teams to agree on the event schema.

speaker: me
text: How did you get them aligned?

speaker: them
text: I wrote a one-page RFC, then spent two weeks doing 1:1s before ever calling a meeting.

speaker: them
text: There was one tech lead who really pushed back — thought event sourcing was overkill.

speaker: them
text: We prototyped both for two weeks and let the numbers decide. He ended up championing it.
